title: Align auth env vars + precedence (explicit params > env) and add redaction-safe auth errors
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Python SDK: standardized auth resolution order (explicit params win), aligned env var names with cross-SDK standard, deprecated legacy env vars with warning, and ensured auth-related errors never include secrets.
pr_body: Context: This is part of the cross-language SDK parity initiative (ENG-5122) to make authentication behavior consistent across Python/TS/Go and reduce support churn from “works in TS but not Python” reports. This PR updates the Python SDK’s auth resolution logic to match the agreed standard: explicit client arguments override environment variables, env vars follow a single documented precedence, and auth failures must be redaction-safe. Summary of changes: (1) Auth resolution order: Client(api_key=..., bearer_token=...) > env vars > error. If both api_key and bearer_token are provided explicitly, bearer_token wins (because it maps to Authorization: Bearer and is unambiguous); we emit a debug-level note (redaction-safe) to clarify which was used. If neither is provided explicitly, we check env vars in precedence order: REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN, then REDWOOD_API_KEY. (2) Backwards compatibility: Legacy env vars are still read but deprecated with a warning that includes the replacement name and upgrade guidance; legacy names supported: REDWOOD_API_TOKEN (maps to bearer), REDWOOD_KEY (maps to api_key). The warning is emitted once per process to avoid noisy logs. (3) Header formatting: bearer_token -> Authorization: Bearer <token>; api_key -> Authorization: Bearer <key> (existing gateway behavior), but we now keep the internal “source” field so error messages can say “from env var REDWOOD_API_KEY” without printing the value. (4) Redaction-safe errors: Auth-related exceptions and debug logs never include the raw secret. We only ever show: the source (explicit/env var name) and a fingerprint (last4 + length), e.g. “len=51 last4=abcd”. (5) Docstrings & docs: Updated Client() docstring + module-level docs to list env var names and precedence explicitly, plus examples showing explicit parameter usage for production. (6) Tests: Added unit tests covering precedence, legacy env var migration warnings, whitespace trimming, and ensuring no secret value is present in exception strings. Notes/Non-goals: No API surface redesign; no new auth mechanisms; no changes to request signing. This PR is narrowly scoped to resolution order + safe messaging to satisfy security review and parity matrix acceptance criteria.
commits: sdk/auth: introduce AuthResolver with explicit > env precedence
sdk/auth: support legacy env vars with one-time deprecation warnings
sdk/errors: redact secrets in auth-related exceptions + debug logs
docs: update Client() docstring + README auth section
changed_files: redwood/_http.py (propagate auth source metadata for diagnostics)
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can you confirm we match the proposed standard exactly? Specifically: explicit params always win; env vars use REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN then REDWOOD_API_KEY; legacy env vars allowed but warned. Also please add a test that verifies warnings are emitted once per process.

Sabrina James: Confirmed. Implemented precedence as discussed, added REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN > REDWOOD_API_KEY ordering, and kept REDWOOD_API_TOKEN/REDWOOD_KEY as deprecated. Added a one-time warning gate via a module-level flag + test asserting only one warning across multiple Client constructions.

Marcus Lin: Security nit: don’t include token length if it could be used as an identifier across logs (low risk but avoid). Also ensure exception messages never include env var *values* even if they contain whitespace or quotes. Please add a test that sets REDWOOD_API_KEY to a known string and asserts it doesn’t appear anywhere in raised error strings.

Sabrina James: Good catch. I removed the length from user-visible exception text; kept it in debug logs behind a structured logger field, but that field is now hashed (sha256 truncated) rather than length. Added tests for whitespace/quotes and for absence of the raw token value in exception strings and repr().

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Platform expectation: both api_key and bearer_token flow through Authorization: Bearer today. The client should still accept api_key as a param for backwards compatibility but we should document bearer_token as preferred terminology. Also, if both explicit api_key and env bearer_token are set, explicit must win even if env bearer_token exists.
Sabrina James: Agreed. Updated docs to recommend bearer_token terminology; api_key remains supported. Added a test for explicit api_key winning over env bearer token.

Monica Patel: Please add a short migration note to the changelog about env var renames and the deprecation timeline (no removal date yet, but state “will be removed in a future major version”). Also link ENG-5122 in the PR body.
Sabrina James: Done—added changelog entry + migration note and linked ENG-5122/ENG-5120 in the description.
Ibrahim Khan: Final pass looks good. Approving.
Marcus Lin: Approved after redaction changes and tests.
Monica Patel: Approved. Let’s ensure TS/Go match these names exactly before we announce.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main; commit message: "Align auth env vars + precedence; redaction-safe auth errors"
notes_for_release_coordination: This PR introduces deprecation warnings for legacy env vars; coordinate with docs/migration guide to avoid surprise. No runtime behavior change for users who pass api_key/bearer_token explicitly; only env var precedence changes could affect users with multiple env vars set.
